claim: SMAD4 is expressed in primordial follicles, growing follicles, and granulosa cells collected from pre-antral follicles.
source: As shown in Figure 1A and consistent with prior reports, SMAD4 was detectable in primordial and growing follicles as well as in the granulosa cells collected from pre-antral follicles.
evidence: Supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 1A and consistent with prior reports.

claim: SMAD2 and SMAD3 are present in follicles, with SMAD2 being the major species detected in oocytes.
source: SMAD2 and SMAD3 were also present, with SMAD2 being the major species detected in oocytes.
evidence: Supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Amhr2-Cre does not mediate efficient recombination of floxed DNA in granulosa cells in this system.
source: Thus, in our system, Amhr2-Cre did not mediate efficient recombination of floxed DNA in granulosa cells.
evidence: Supported by observation that less than 10% of FACS-sorted granulosa cells were GFP-positive (Figure 1C) and consistent with previous reports.

claim: Less than 10% of FACS-sorted granulosa cells were GFP-positive in Amhr2-Cre mice.
source: Consistent with this observation, less than 10% of FACS-sorted granulosa cells were GFP-positive (Figure 1C, right).
evidence: Supported by FACS analysis data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The in vitro ER-Cre strategy results in a substantial fraction of granulosa cells undergoing Cre-mediated recombination.
source: Under these conditions, a substantial fraction of the granulosa cells underwent Cre-mediated recombination, as indicated by the expression of GFP in immunostained GOCs and by FACS analysis (Figure 1E).
evidence: Supported by GFP expression in immunostained GOCs and FACS analysis shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Following tamoxifen treatment and culture, there was an approximately 60% reduction in the number of Smad4 mRNA foci in granulosa cells from ER-Cre+; Smad4fl/fl mice compared to ER-Cre-; Smad4fl/fl mice.
source: Following tamoxifen treatment and culture, there was an approximately 60% reduction in the number of foci in the granulosa cells from 5.78+/-0.36 (mean, SEM, n=21) in ER-Cre-; Smad4fl/fl mice to 2.16+/-0.26 (n=26) in ER-Cre+; Smad4fl/fl mice (p<0.0001)
evidence: Supported by RNAscope data shown in Figure 1F with statistical significance p<0.0001.

claim: There was a 70% reduction in the amount of Smad4 mRNA in granulosa cells from ER-Cre+; Smad4fl/fl mice compared to controls.
source: and a 70% reduction in the amount of PCR product from granulosa cells (n=5, p=0.0001) (Figure 1F).
evidence: Supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1F with statistical significance p=0.0001.

claim: Immunoblotting revealed a 70% reduction in SMAD4 protein in the granulosa cells of ER-Cre+; Smad4fl/fl mice compared to ER-Cre-; Smad4fl/fl controls.
source: Immunoblotting of granulosa cells revealed a corresponding 70% reduction in SMAD4 protein in the granulosa cells of ER-Cre+; Smad4fl/fl mice compared to ER-Cre-; Smad4fl/fl controls (n=11, p<0.0001) (Figure 1G).
evidence: Supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 1G with statistical significance p<0.0001.

claim: The in vitro ER-Cre strategy substantially reduced although did not eliminate SMAD4 from the granulosa cells.
source: Thus, the in vitro ER-Cre strategy substantially reduced although did not eliminate SMAD4 from the granulosa cells.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the 70% reduction in SMAD4 protein observed in immunoblotting experiments.

claim: There was a 20.4% reduction in the number of TZPs in GOCs from Smad4fl/fl mice compared to controls.
source: We observed a 20.4+/-0.05% reduction in the number of TZPs in the GOCs from the Smad4fl/fl mice (n=63 [control], 59 [experimental], p=0.002).
evidence: Supported by TZP counting data from intact GOCs with statistical significance p=0.002.

claim: The mean oocyte diameter did not differ between control and Smad4fl/fl groups in intact GOCs.
source: TZP number was normalized to the diameter of the corresponding oocyte, although the mean oocyte diameter did not differ between the groups (Figure 2B)
evidence: Supported by oocyte diameter measurements shown in Figure 2B.

claim: There was a 51.1% reduction in the normalized number of TZPs in denuded GOCs from Smad4fl/fl mice compared to controls.
source: This analysis revealed a striking 51.1+/-0.04% reduction in the normalized number of TZPs in the GOCs from the Smad4fl/fl mice (n=44 [control], 47 [experimental], p<0.0001) (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: Supported by TZP counting data from denuded GOCs with statistical significance p<0.0001.

claim: There was a 43.6% decrease in TZPs in ER-Cre+; Smad4fl/fl mice compared to ER-Cre-; Smad4fl/fl mice following tamoxifen treatment and culture.
source: A quantitatively similar 43.6+/-0.04% decrease in TZPs within the ER-Cre+ population ( +=164 [control], 172 [experimental], p<0.0001) (Figure 2D) was observed following tamoxifen treatment and culture.
evidence: Supported by TZP counting data comparing different control genotypes with statistical significance p<0.0001.

claim: Depletion of SMAD4 in the granulosa cells is associated with a decrease in the number of TZPs.
source: Together, these results indicate that depletion of SMAD4 in the granulosa cells is associated with a decrease in the number of TZPs.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from multiple TZP counting experiments showing reductions of 20-50%.

claim: Despite the decreased number of TZPs, depletion of SMAD4 did not detectably impair gap junctional communication between the granulosa cells and the oocyte.
source: Thus, despite the decreased number of TZPs, depletion of SMAD4 did not detectably impair gap junctional communication between the granulosa cells and the oocyte.
evidence: Supported by FRAP assay data showing no difference in fluorescence recovery between groups (Figure 2E).

claim: There was no difference between control and Smad4fl/fl groups in the rate of transfer of fluorescence from the granulosa cells to the oocyte in FRAP assays.
source: As shown in Figure 2E, which plots the fluorescence in the oocyte as a function of time after photobleaching and at the end of the recording period normalized to the initial fluorescence, we observed no difference between groups in the rate of transfer of fluorescence from the granulosa cells to the oocyte.
evidence: Supported by FRAP assay data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The reduced number of TZPs in ER-Cre+; Smad4fl/fl complexes was not due to impaired proliferation of the granulosa cells.
source: No difference between the groups in the fraction of EdU-positive cells was observed (Figure 2F), however, implying that the reduced number of TZPs was not due to impaired proliferation of the granulosa cells.
evidence: Supported by EdU incorporation assay data shown in Figure 2F showing no difference in proliferation.

claim: There was a 25% decrease in the mean volume of Smad4fl/fl granulosa cells compared to wild-type cells.
source: We observed a 25% decrease in the mean volume of Smad4fl/fl granulosa cells compared to wild-type cells (323.2+/-11.2 vs 242.6+/-10.0; n=293, 322; p<0.0001)
evidence: Supported by 3D image analysis data with statistical significance p<0.0001.

claim: There was no difference between genotypes in the sphericity of granulosa cells.
source: but no difference between genotypes in the sphericity of the cells (Figure 3C).
evidence: Supported by 3D image analysis data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Wild-type cells harbored a mean of 15.8 TZPs per cell, which was reduced by 35% in Smad4fl/fl cells to 10.5 TZPs per cell.
source: However, whereas wild-type cells harbored a mean of 15.8+/-0.87 (n=55) TZPs per cell, this number was reduced by 35% in Smad4fl/fl cells to 10.5+/-0.71 (n=65, p<0.0001).
evidence: Supported by 3D image analysis of individual GFP-positive cells with statistical significance p<0.0001.

claim: TZPs of Smad4fl/fl cells were about 10% longer than those of wild-type cells.
source: As compared to those of wild-type cells, the TZPs of the Smad4fl/fl cells were about 10% longer (4.64+/-0.08 μm vs 5.19+/-0.09 μm; n=893, 720; p<0.0001)
evidence: Supported by 3D image analysis of TZP morphology with statistical significance p<0.0001.

claim: TZPs of Smad4fl/fl cells were very slightly narrower than those of wild-type cells.
source: and very slightly narrower (0.40+/-0.003 μm vs 0.38+/-0.003 μm; n=870, 719; p<0.0001)(Figure 3E).
evidence: Supported by 3D image analysis of TZP morphology with statistical significance p<0.0001.

claim: The number of TZPs is reduced in individual SMAD4-depleted granulosa cells.
source: These results obtained using reconstructed 3-dimensional images of GFP-positive cells establish that the number of TZPs is reduced in individual SMAD4-depleted granulosa cells.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from 3D image analysis showing 35% reduction in TZPs per cell.

claim: There was a ~30% reduction in mean volume of Smad4fl/fl granulosa cells compared to Smad4wt/wt cells in reaggregated GOCs.
source: When the entire population of granulosa cells in the reaggregated GOCs was analyzed, there was a ~30% reduction in mean volume in the Smad4fl/fl cells as compared to Smad4wt/wt cells (394.5+/-18.8 vs 279.8+/-16.6; n=185, 159; p<0.0001)
evidence: Supported by 3D image analysis of reaggregated GOCs with statistical significance p<0.0001.

claim: There was no difference in cell sphericity between genotypes in reaggregated GOCs.
source: and no difference in cell sphericity (Figure 4C), as observed using intact GOCs.
evidence: Supported by 3D image analysis data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The mean number of TZPs per cell was reduced by ~50% in Smad4fl/fl cells compared to Smad4wt/wt cells in reaggregated GOCs.
source: Within this group, the mean number of TZPs per cell was reduced by ~50%, from 14.2+/-2.0 (n=16) in the Smad4wt/wt cells to 6.84+/-1.1 (n=25) in the Smad4fl/fl cells (Figure 4D, p=0.001).
evidence: Supported by 3D image analysis of reaggregated GOCs with statistical significance p=0.001.

claim: There was a ~20% increase in the mean length of the TZPs of Smad4fl/fl cells compared to wild-type cells in reaggregated GOCs.
source: A ~20% increase in the mean length of the TZPs of Smad4fl/fl cells (3.71+/-0.17 vs 4.40+/-0.28; n=174, 154; p=0.03) was also detected, as in intact GOCs
evidence: Supported by 3D image analysis of reaggregated GOCs with statistical significance p=0.03.

claim: There was no difference in the mean width of TZPs between genotypes in reaggregated GOCs.
source: but no difference in the mean width (Figure 4E).
evidence: Supported by 3D image analysis data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The mean difference between the distance from the origin and the tip of TZPs to the oocyte surface was 50% greater in Smad4fl/fl cells compared to Smad4wt/wt cells.
source: This analysis revealed that the mean difference was 50% greater in the Smad4fl/fl cells compared to Smad4wt/wt cells (1.61+/-0.16 vs 2.40+/-0.21; n=174, 157; p=0.003) (Figure 4G).
evidence: Supported by TZP trajectory analysis with statistical significance p=0.003.

claim: The tips of the TZPs of the Smad4fl/fl cells were, on average, closer to the oocyte than those of the Smad4wt/wt cells.
source: This indicates that the tips of the TZPs of the Smad4fl/fl cells were, on average, closer to the oocyte than those of the Smad4wt/wt cells.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from trajectory analysis showing 50% greater mean difference in distances.

claim: The proportion of TZPs that were oriented away from the oocyte trended towards being greater in the Smad4wt/wt cells, although the difference did not reach statistical significance.
source: We also found that the proportion of TZPs that were oriented away from the oocyte trended towards being greater in the Smad4wt/wt cells, although the difference did not reach statistical significance (Figure 4G).
evidence: Supported by TZP trajectory analysis shown in Figure 4G, but without statistical significance.

claim: SMAD4 was reduced by 73.5% in Smad4fl/fl granulosa cells.
source: Consistent with the previous results (see Figure 1E), SMAD4 was reduced by 73.5+/-0.05% in the Smad4fl/fl granulosa cells (Figure 5A, n=6, p<0.0001).
evidence: Supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 5A with statistical significance p<0.0001.

claim: N-cadherin was reduced by 52.7% in Smad4fl/fl granulosa cells.
source: Strikingly, N-cadherin was reduced by 52.7+/-0.04% (n=6, p=0.0004) in the Smad4fl/fl granulosa cells (Figure 5A).
evidence: Supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 5A with statistical significance p=0.0004.

claim: Notch2 was reduced by 52.6% in Smad4fl/fl granulosa cells.
source: Moreover, Notch2, a transmembrane receptor expressed in granulosa cells that associates with membrane-bound Jagged1 expressed on the oocyte, was reduced by 52.6+/-0.05% (n=5; p=0.0003) in these cells (Figure 5B).
evidence: Supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 5B with statistical significance p=0.0003.

claim: There was no detectable reduction in the amount of Cdh2 or Notch2 mRNA in Smad4fl/fl granulosa cells compared to controls.
source: In contrast to the protein, however, there was no detectable reduction in the amount of encoding mRNA in either case as assayed using qRT-PCR, although Smad4 was reduced in the same samples (Figure 5C).
evidence: Supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: A reduction in SMAD4 in granulosa cells is associated with a reduction in certain transmembrane proteins, including those responsible for cell adhesion.
source: Thus, a reduction in SMAD4 in granulosa cells is associated with a reduction in certain transmembrane proteins, including those responsible for cell adhesion.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from observations of reduced N-cadherin and Notch2 protein levels in SMAD4-depleted cells.

claim: Myo10, Fscn1, and Daam1 mRNAs were not depleted in Smad4fl/fl granulosa cells compared to Smad4wt/wt cells.
source: We found that they were not depleted in the Smad4fl/fl granulosa cells compared to the Smad4wt/wt cells (Figure 5D).
evidence: Supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Either the SMAD4 which remained was sufficient to induce expression of Myo10, Fscn1, and Daam1 genes or GDF9 regulates their expression through a SMAD4-independent pathway.
source: This implies either that the SMAD4 which remained was sufficient to induce expression of these genes or the GDF9 regulates their expression through a SMAD4-independent pathway.
evidence: Speculative interpretation of the observation that Myo10, Fscn1, and Daam1 mRNAs were not depleted despite SMAD4 reduction.

claim: Development of the mammalian oocyte requires physical contact with the surrounding granulosa cells of the follicle.
source: Development of the mammalian oocyte requires physical contact with the surrounding granulosa cells of the follicle, which provide it with essential nutrients and regulatory signals.
evidence: Supported by multiple citations in the Introduction section.

claim: Contact between oocyte and granulosa cells is achieved through specialized filopodia, termed transzonal projections (TZPs), that extend from the granulosa cells to the oocyte surface.
source: This contact is achieved through specialized filopodia, termed transzonal projections (TZPs), that extend from the granulosa cells to the oocyte surface.
evidence: Established knowledge about TZP structure and function.

claim: Transforming growth factor (TGFβ) family ligands produced by the oocyte increase the number of TZPs.
source: Transforming growth factor (TGFβ) family ligands produced by the oocyte increase the number of TZPs, but how they do so is unknown.
evidence: Stated as known fact in the Abstract, with the mechanism being unknown.

claim: There was a 20–50% decrease in the total number of TZPs in SMAD4-depleted granulosa cell-oocyte complexes.
source: We observed a 20–50% decrease in the total number of TZPs in SMAD4-depleted granulosa cell-oocyte complexes
evidence: Summary statement in Abstract supported by data from multiple experimental approaches.

claim: There was a 50% decrease in the number of newly generated TZPs when SMAD4-depleted granulosa cells were reaggregated with wild-type oocytes.
source: and a 50% decrease in the number of newly generated TZPs when the granulosa cells were reaggregated with wild-type oocytes.
evidence: Summary statement in Abstract supported by reaggregation assay data.

claim: TZPs of SMAD4-depleted cells were longer than controls.
source: Three-dimensional image analysis revealed that TZPs of SMAD4-depleted cells were longer than controls
evidence: Summary statement in Abstract supported by 3D image analysis data.

claim: TZPs of SMAD4-depleted cells were more frequently oriented towards the oocyte.
source: and more frequently oriented towards the oocyte.
evidence: Summary statement in Abstract supported by trajectory analysis data.

claim: N-cadherin and Notch2 were reduced by 50% in SMAD4-depleted cells.
source: Strikingly, the transmembrane proteins, N-cadherin and Notch2, were reduced by 50% in SMAD4-depleted cells.
evidence: Summary statement in Abstract supported by immunoblot data.

claim: SMAD4 may modulate a network of cell adhesion proteins that stabilize the attachment of TZPs to the oocyte, thereby amplifying signalling between the two cell types.
source: SMAD4 may thus modulate a network of cell adhesion proteins that stabilize the attachment of TZPs to the oocyte, thereby amplifying signalling between the two cell types.
evidence: Proposed model based on experimental observations of reduced N-cadherin and Notch2 and altered TZP characteristics.

claim: Signals from the granulosa cells initiate the increase in the volume of the oocyte when primordial (non-growing) follicles are activated to enter the growth phase.
source: Signals from the granulosa cells initiate the increase in the volume of the oocyte when primordial (non-growing) follicles are activated to enter the growth phase (Zhang et al., 2014; Saatcioglu et al., 2016; Nagamatsu et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to Zhang et al., 2014; Saatcioglu et al., 2016; Nagamatsu et al., 2019.

claim: The granulosa cells provide nucleotides, amino acids, and pyruvate to the growing oocyte via gap junctions that connect the two cell types.
source: Subsequently, the granulosa cells provide nucleotides, amino acids, and pyruvate to the growing oocyte via gap junctions that connect the two cell types (Xie et al., 2023; Clarke, 2018; Marchais et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citations to Xie et al., 2023; Clarke, 2018; Marchais et al., 2022.

claim: When gap junctional communication between granulosa cells and oocytes is genetically disrupted, oocytes do not develop normally and cannot be fertilized.
source: When gap junctional communication between the two cell types is genetically disrupted, oocytes do not develop normally and cannot be fertilized (Gittens and Kidder, 2005; Simon et al., 1997; Winterhager and Kidder, 2015; Carabatsos et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by citations to Gittens and Kidder, 2005; Simon et al., 1997; Winterhager and Kidder, 2015; Carabatsos et al., 2000.

claim: Once the oocyte reaches full size, it acquires the ability to undergo meiotic maturation, but is prevented from precociously doing so by cyclic GMP that is produced and transferred to it by the granulosa cells via gap junctions.
source: Once the oocyte reaches full size, it acquires the ability to undergo the final stage of development, termed meiotic maturation, but is prevented from precociously doing so by cyclic GMP that is produced and transferred to it by the granulosa cells, also via gap junctions (Jaffe and Egbert, 2017; Wigglesworth et al., 2013; Norris et al., 2009; Zhang et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to Jaffe and Egbert, 2017; Wigglesworth et al., 2013; Norris et al., 2009; Zhang et al., 2010.

claim: In vitro, oocytes can develop normally when enclosed by granulosa cells but not when the granulosa cells are removed and provided in co-culture.
source: In vitro, oocytes can develop normally when enclosed by granulosa cells but not when the granulosa cells are removed and provided in co-culture, further emphasizing the crucial importance of physical contact between the two cell types (O'Brien et al., 2003; Eppig, 1979; Herta et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to O'Brien et al., 2003; Eppig, 1979; Herta et al., 2021.

claim: In primordial follicles, a single layer of squamous granulosa cells surrounds the oocyte and contact it via adherens junctions.
source: In primordial follicles, a single layer of squamous granulosa cells surrounds the oocyte and contact it via adherens junctions (Mora et al., 2012; Jorgensen, 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to Mora et al., 2012; Jorgensen, 2013.

claim: Following activation of growth, a glycoprotein-rich coat termed the zona pellucida becomes established around the oocyte.
source: Following activation of growth, a glycoprotein-rich coat termed the zona pellucida becomes established around the oocyte (Litscher and Wassarman, 2020; Wassarman and Litscher, 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Litscher and Wassarman, 2020; Wassarman and Litscher, 2018.

claim: The zona pellucida steadily thickens as growth continues, reaching a final thickness of about 7 μm in mice and 15 μm in humans.
source: The zona pellucida steadily thickens as growth continues, reaching a final thickness of about 7 μm in mice and 15 μm in humans.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge about zona pellucida development.

claim: Despite the barrier imposed by the zona pellucida, the granulosa cells and oocyte maintain direct contact by a dense network of thin filopodia-like projections, termed transzonal projections (TZPs), that grow out from the granulosa cells through the zona pellucida.
source: Despite the barrier imposed by the zona pellucida, the granulosa cells and oocyte maintain direct contact by a dense network of thin filopodia-like projections, termed transzonal projections (TZPs), that grow out from the granulosa cells through the zona pellucida (Clarke, 2022; Macaulay et al., 2014; Baena and Terasaki, 2019; Motta et al., 1994; Zhang et al., 2021; Albertini and Rider, 1994).
evidence: Supported by citations to Clarke, 2022; Macaulay et al., 2014; Baena and Terasaki, 2019; Motta et al., 1994; Zhang et al., 2021; Albertini and Rider, 1994.

claim: The tips of the TZPs establish contact with the oocyte plasma membrane through heterotypic adherens junctions comprising N-cadherin (granulosa cell) and E-cadherin (oocyte) and harbour the gap junctions that link the two cell types.
source: The tips of the TZPs establish contact with the oocyte plasma membrane through heterotypic adherens junctions comprising N-cadherin (granulosa cell) and E-cadherin (oocyte) and harbour the gap junctions that link the two cell types (Mora et al., 2012) and likely also through focal adhesions (McGinnis and Kinsey, 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to Mora et al., 2012 and McGinnis and Kinsey, 2015.

claim: New TZPs are generated throughout follicular growth, thereby increasing intercellular molecular trafficking.
source: New TZPs are generated throughout follicular growth, thereby increasing intercellular molecular trafficking (El-Hayek et al., 2018a).
evidence: Supported by citation to El-Hayek et al., 2018a.

claim: A genetically imposed decrease in the number of TZPs leads to defects in oocyte gene expression and to abnormal meiotic maturation and embryonic development.
source: A genetically imposed decrease in the number of TZPs leads to defects in oocyte gene expression and to abnormal meiotic maturation and embryonic development (Crozet et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citation to Crozet et al., 2023.

claim: The TGFβ signalling pathway regulates the functions and interactions of a wide range of cell types under various physiological and pathological conditions.
source: The TGFβ signalling pathway regulates the functions and interactions of a wide range of cell types under various physiological and pathological conditions (Derynck and Budi, 2019; Peng et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citations to Derynck and Budi, 2019; Peng et al., 2022.

claim: Binding of the TGFβ ligand to a complex of type I and type II receptors located at the cell surface activates signalling within the cell, most commonly through the members of the SMAD family of transcription factors.
source: Binding of the ligand to a complex of type I and type II receptors located at the cell surface activates signalling within the cell, most commonly through the members of the SMAD family of transcription factors, although SMAD-independent signalling can also occur (Aashaq et al., 2022; Derynck and Budi, 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to Aashaq et al., 2022; Derynck and Budi, 2019.

claim: Upon phosphorylation of the tetrameric type II and type I receptors and subsequent phosphorylation of receptor-activated SMAD proteins (R-SMADs), a heterotrimeric complex with SMAD4 is formed which enters the nucleus and regulates gene expression by binding to specific SMAD-binding DNA elements.
source: Upon phosphorylation of the tetrameric type II and type I receptors and subsequent phosphorylation of receptor-activated SMAD proteins (R-SMADs; SMAD1, 2, 3, 5, and 8), a heterotrimeric complex with SMAD4 is formed which enters the nucleus and regulates gene expression by binding to specific SMAD-binding DNA elements.
evidence: Established knowledge about TGFβ/SMAD signaling mechanism.

claim: Although R-SMADs can signal in the absence of SMAD4, evidence indicates that the presence of SMAD4 in the heterotrimer amplifies TGFβ cell signalling by stabilizing the complex and by favouring the binding of other transcriptional co-repressors or co-activators of target genes.
source: Although R-SMADs can signal in the absence of SMAD4, evidence indicates that the presence of SMAD4 in the heterotrimer amplifies TGFβ cell signalling by stabilizing the complex and by favouring the binding of other transcriptional co-repressors or co-activators of target genes (Aragón et al., 2019; Guglielmi et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to Aragón et al., 2019; Guglielmi et al., 2021.

claim: TGFβ signalling via SMAD3 in granulosa cells acts initially in primordial follicles to maintain their quiescence.
source: TGFβ signalling via SMAD3 in granulosa cells acts initially in primordial follicles to maintain their quiescence (Granados-Aparici et al., 2019; Kang et al., 2014)
evidence: Supported by citations to Granados-Aparici et al., 2019; Kang et al., 2014.

claim: Following activation of primordial follicles, TGFβ signalling becomes excluded from the nucleus in association with rapid granulosa cell growth and proliferation.
source: and later, following their activation, becomes excluded from the nucleus in association with rapid granulosa cell growth and proliferation (Hardy et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Hardy et al., 2018.

claim: GDF9 signals through SMAD2/3.
source: The TGFβ superfamily members, growth-differentiation factor (GDF) 9, which signals through SMAD2/3
evidence: Established knowledge about GDF9 signaling pathway.

claim: BMP15 signals through SMAD1/5/8.
source: and bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) 15, which signals through SMAD1/5/8
evidence: Established knowledge about BMP15 signaling pathway.

claim: GDF9 and BMP15 are produced by the oocyte.
source: The TGFβ superfamily members, growth-differentiation factor (GDF) 9, which signals through SMAD2/3, and bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) 15, which signals through SMAD1/5/8, are produced by the oocyte (Dong et al., 1996; Yan et al., 2001).
evidence: Supported by citations to Dong et al., 1996; Yan et al., 2001.

claim: Female mice lacking GDF9 rarely generate more than a single layer of granulosa cells.
source: Female mice lacking GDF9 rarely generate more than a single layer of granulosa cells (Elvin et al., 1999b; Elvin et al., 1999a; Dong et al., 1996).
evidence: Supported by citations to Elvin et al., 1999b; Elvin et al., 1999a; Dong et al., 1996.

claim: The defect in follicular development in GDF9-deficient mice can be rescued by preventing the production of inhibin, and the doubly mutant follicles can develop at least to the pre-antral stage.
source: This defect can be rescued by preventing the production of inhibin, and the doubly mutant follicles can develop at least to the pre-antral stage (Wu et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citation to Wu et al., 2004.

claim: Genetic inactivation of SMAD4 in the granulosa cells from growing follicles leads to a reduction in the number of antral follicles and ovulated eggs, as well as the appearance of luteinized follicles containing entrapped oocytes.
source: Genetic inactivation of SMAD4 in the granulosa cells from growing follicles leads to a reduction in the number of antral follicles and ovulated eggs, as well as the appearance of luteinized follicles containing entrapped oocytes (Pangas et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation to Pangas et al., 2006.

claim: Similar phenotypes are observed when both SMAD2 and SMAD3 are inactivated in the granulosa cells.
source: Similar phenotypes are observed when both SMAD2 and SMAD3 are inactivated in the granulosa cells (Li et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to Li et al., 2008.

claim: The effects of SMAD4 inactivation are likely due at least in part to a failure of the cumulus layer to expand in response to the ovulatory surge of LH.
source: These effects are likely due at least in part to a failure of the cumulus layer to expand in response to the ovulatory surge of LH (Pangas et al., 2006; Li et al., 2008), as expansion is known to require SMAD signalling and to be required for ovulation (Dragovic et al., 2007; Hao et al., 2022; Mottershead et al., 2015; Peng et al., 2013; Yu et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to Pangas et al., 2006; Li et al., 2008; Dragovic et al., 2007; Hao et al., 2022; Mottershead et al., 2015; Peng et al., 2013; Yu et al., 2013.

claim: Deletion of GDF9 leads to both a decrease in the number of TZPs and a failure of a proportion of the TZPs to correctly orient towards the oocyte.
source: First, deletion of GDF9 leads to both a decrease in the number of TZPs and a failure of a proportion of the TZPs to correctly orient towards the oocyte (Carabatsos et al., 1998).
evidence: Supported by citation to Carabatsos et al., 1998.

claim: TZP number is reduced in follicles grown in vitro following RNAi-mediated depletion of GDF9 in the oocyte.
source: Second, TZP number is reduced in follicles grown in vitro following RNAi-mediated depletion of GDF9 in the oocyte (El-Hayek et al., 2018a).
evidence: Supported by citation to El-Hayek et al., 2018a.

claim: Depletion of SMAD4 in the granulosa cells decreases the number of TZPs that project from individual granulosa cells in both intact granulosa cell-oocyte complexes (GOCs) and in reaggregated complexes.
source: Using image analysis tools and three-dimensional reconstructions, we show that depletion of SMAD4 in the granulosa cells decreases the number of TZPs that project from individual granulosa cells in both intact granulosa cell-oocyte complexes (GOCs) and in reaggregated complexes.
evidence: Summary statement supported by multiple experimental approaches including 3D image analysis.

claim: Morphometric parameters including length and orientation of TZPs are altered in SMAD4-depleted cells.
source: Morphometric parameters including length and orientation are also altered.
evidence: Summary statement supported by 3D image analysis and trajectory analysis data.

claim: The decrease in TZP number in intact GOCs is associated with a reduction in the amount of N-cadherin and Notch2 in the granulosa cells.
source: The decrease in TZP number in intact GOCs is associated with a reduction in the amount of N-cadherin and Notch2 in the granulosa cells, suggesting that the composition of the granulosa cell surface is perturbed in the absence of SMAD4.
evidence: Supported by immunoblot data showing 50% reduction in N-cadherin and Notch2.

claim: SMAD4, through its activity to increase expression of target genes, stabilizes TZPs by promoting their adhesion to the oocyte surface, thereby helping to increase the number of TZPs and communication between the growing oocyte and its follicular microenvironment.
source: We propose that SMAD4, through its activity to increase expression of target genes, stabilizes TZPs by promoting their adhesion to the oocyte surface, thereby helping to increase the number of TZPs and communication between the growing oocyte and its follicular microenvironment.
evidence: Proposed model based on experimental observations of reduced N-cadherin, altered TZP characteristics, and easier removal of TZPs in SMAD4-depleted cells.

claim: The observation that TZP-number was modestly reduced when intact GOCs were analyzed, yet markedly reduced when oocytes from which the granulosa cells had been stripped were analyzed, suggested that the attachment between the TZPs and oocyte might be weakened when SMAD4 was depleted.
source: The observation that TZP-number was modestly reduced when intact GOCs were analyzed, yet markedly reduced when oocytes from which the granulosa cells had been stripped were analyzed, suggested that the attachment between the TZPs and oocyte might be weakened when SMAD4 was depleted.
evidence: Inference drawn from comparing TZP counts in intact vs. denuded GOCs (20% vs. 51% reduction).

claim: By increasing the quantity of N-cadherin in the granulosa cells, SMAD4 increases the strength of adhesion of the TZPs to the oocyte surface.
source: We propose that, by increasing the quantity of N-cadherin in the granulosa cells, SMAD4 increases the strength of adhesion of the TZPs to the oocyte surface (Figure 6).
evidence: Proposed mechanism based on observation of reduced N-cadherin in SMAD4-depleted cells.

claim: Increased strength of TZP adhesion to the oocyte surface would decrease the probability of retraction, thereby increasing the steady-state number of TZPs.
source: This in turn would decrease the probability of retraction, thereby increasing the steady-state number of TZPs.
evidence: Logical inference from the proposed model of SMAD4 function.

claim: If the ability of the TZPs to establish a stable contact with the oocyte were impaired in SMAD4-depleted cells, a relatively large proportion might continue to 'search' for an attachment and to lengthen during the searching process.
source: Specifically, if the ability of the TZPs to establish a stable contact with the oocyte wer impaired in SMAD4-depleted cells, a relatively large proportion might continue to 'search' for an attachment and to lengthen during the searching process.
evidence: Speculative explanation for the observation that non-attached TZPs of SMAD4-depleted cells were longer and closer to the oocyte.

claim: Some reports have linked SMAD4 to transcription of the Cdh2 gene, which encodes N-cadherin.
source: Mechanistically, some reports have linked SMAD4 to transcription of the Cdh2, which encodes N-cadherin (Kang et al., 2014; Yang et al., 2015)
evidence: Supported by citations to Kang et al., 2014; Yang et al., 2015.

claim: SMAD4 might act more broadly to regulate the expression of genes whose products maintain the normal configuration of the granulosa cell plasma membrane.
source: In view of the reduced quantity in the latter of Notch2, also a membrane-associated protein, it may be speculated that SMAD4 might act more broadly to regulate the expression of genes whose products maintain the normal configuration of the granulosa cell plasma membrane.
evidence: Speculative interpretation based on observation that both N-cadherin and Notch2 were reduced.

claim: Granulosa-cell depletion of SMAD4 is associated with the presence of follicles containing luteinized granulosa cells enclosing an entrapped oocyte and increased expression of markers of luteinization.
source: An alternative explanation is raised by observations that granulosa-cell depletion of SMAD4 is associated with the presence of follicles containing luteinized granulosa cells enclosing an entrapped oocyte and increased expression of markers of luteinization, including Cyp11a1, Sfrp4, Star, and Ptgfr (Pangas et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation to Pangas et al., 2006.

claim: The SMAD4-depleted granulosa cells in the GOCs studied did not become luteinized under the experimental conditions.
source: We did not detect increased expression of the luteinization markers (unpublished data), suggesting that luteinization did not occur under the conditions of our experiments.
evidence: Supported by unpublished data showing no increased expression of luteinization markers.

claim: The number of TZPs that project from an individual granulosa cell is about 15 in mid-growth stage follicles and about 40 in antral follicles.
source: Regardless of the mechanism linking SMAD4 to TZP number, it is noteworthy that the number of TZPs that project from an individual granulosa cells – about 15 in this study and about 40 in a previous study where more advanced (antral) follicles were examined (Baena and Terasaki, 2019)
evidence: Supported by data from this study and citation to Baena and Terasaki, 2019.

claim: The number of TZPs per granulosa cell considerably exceeds the number of filopodia that are present on individual blastomeres of mouse embryos (5-6) or on chick embryonic cells (~4).
source: – considerably exceeds the number of filopodia that are present on individual blastomeres of mouse embryos (5-6) (Fierro-González et al., 2013) or on chick embryonic cells (~4) (Pröls et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to Fierro-González et al., 2013 and Pröls et al., 2015.

claim: SMAD4 may act in granulosa cells to amplify an innate ability to generate filopodia, which become TZPs and increase the efficiency of communication between the growing germ cell and its somatic microenvironment.
source: SMAD4 may, therefore, act in granulosa cells to amplify an innate ability to generate filopodia, which become TZPs and increase the efficiency of communication between the growing germ cell and its somatic microenvironment.
evidence: Speculative interpretation based on the observation that granulosa cells have more TZPs than typical cells have filopodia.

claim: TZPs arise from both the innermost and more distal granulosa cell layers.
source: Because TZPs arise from both the innermost and more distal granulosa cell layers (Baena and Terasaki, 2019)
evidence: Supported by citation to Baena and Terasaki, 2019.

claim: The population of TZPs presumably reflects the net result of the generation of new TZPs and the retraction of existing TZPs, as is the case for filopodia.
source: The population of TZPs presumably reflects the net result of the generation of new TZPs and the retraction of existing TZPs, as is the case for filopodia (Gallop, 2020; Heckman and Plummer, 2013; Mattila and Lappalainen, 2008).
evidence: Inference based on knowledge of filopodia dynamics, supported by citations to Gallop, 2020; Heckman and Plummer, 2013; Mattila and Lappalainen, 2008.

claim: The observation that GFP-expressing granulosa cells in reaggregated complexes generated new TZPs implies that SMAD4 is not required for TZP generation.
source: The observation that GFP-expressing granulosa cells in reaggregated complexes generated new TZPs implies that SMAD4 is not required for this process, although it does not rule out a role in increasing the rate of generation.
evidence: Inference drawn from reaggregation assay data showing that SMAD4-depleted cells can still generate TZPs.

claim: Depletion of GDF9 was associated with a reduction in mRNAs encoding structural components of TZPs – Myo10, Fscn1, and Daam1.
source: As we previously reported that depletion of GDF9, which is secreted by the oocyte and signals in the granulosa cells through SMAD4, was associated with a reduction in mRNAs encoding structural components of TZPs – Myo10, Fscn1, and Daam1 (El-Hayek et al., 2018a)
evidence: Supported by citation to El-Hayek et al., 2018a.

claim: Previous studies where SMAD4, or both SMAD2 and SMAD3, was depleted from granulosa cells described a loose or loss association of the cumulus cells with the oocyte in some follicles.
source: Previous studies where SMAD4, or both SMAD2 and SMAD3, was depleted from granulosa cells described a loose or loss association of the cumulus cells with the oocyte in some follicles (Pangas et al., 2006; Li et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to Pangas et al., 2006; Li et al., 2008.

claim: SMAD4 regulates the size of the population of TZPs in growing follicles.
source: Together these observations suggest that SMAD4 regulates the size of the population of TZPs in growing follicles.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from multiple lines of evidence including current study and previous reports.

claim: Because ER is expressed in pituitary gonadotropes and SMAD4 regulates the transcription of the Fshb gene encoding the β-subunit of follicle-stimulating hormone, the ER-Cre model could not be used in vivo.
source: Because ER is expressed in pituitary gonadotropes and SMAD4 regulates the transcription of the Fshb gene encoding the β-subunit of follicle-stimulating hormone (Li et al., 2018), this model could not be used in vivo.
evidence: Supported by citation to Li et al., 2018 and reasoning about potential confounding effects.
